title: Trade a loop for a HashSet
summary: Turn an O(n²) check into O(n) by remembering what you've seen in a HashSet.

say.never: Picture a sign-in sheet at the shop door. To spot someone signing in twice, you *could* compare every name with every other name: O(n²). Or you could read the names once, top to bottom, and keep a pile of names you've already read. For each new name, ask the pile "have I seen you?". If yes, it's a repeat. If not, add it to the pile and carry on.
say.bit: Instead of comparing every pair, walk the list once and remember what you've seen.

steps.title: A HashSet answers in one step

say.never: That only helps if asking the pile is quick. A `HashSet` is: it files each item by a code worked out from its value, so `contains()` goes straight to the right place, about one step however many items it holds. Compare `ArrayList.contains`, which checks item by item. One loop with a HashSet inside is `n × 1` = **O(n)**.
say.bit: `HashSet.contains` and `add` are about O(1), so one loop using them is O(n).

steps.title: Building a set from a list

say.never: You can also make a set from a whole list at once: `new HashSet<>(list)`. It looks at every item once, so that's O(n), and it drops repeats for you. That's handy when you need to ask "is this in the other list?" many times: turn the other list into a set first.
say.bit: `new HashSet<>(list)` is one O(n) pass and drops repeats.

board.code:
HashSet<String> members = new HashSet<>(roster);
boolean on_team = members.contains("Ada");

steps.title: In your lesson: Trade a loop for a HashSet

say.never: `hasDuplicate` is the sign-in sheet: one loop over the teams, a HashSet of the teams seen so far, and `return true` the moment one is already in it. `teamsInBoth` needs one event's teams in a set, then one loop over the other event. Collect the shared teams in a *second* set, so a team listed twice only counts once. Remember `import java.util.HashSet;` at the top.
say.bit: `hasDuplicate`: one loop plus a seen-set. `teamsInBoth`: set of one event, loop the other, collect matches in a set.
